Reading a goal from its tracking

Source: vignettes/goal-tracking.Rmd
goal-tracking.Rmd

Since 2023-24 the NHL has kept the puck and player tracking behind every goal: about fourteen seconds of every skater, both goalies and the puck, ten frames a second. NHL.com uses it for its goal replays. This vignette reads one goal end to end, Connor McDavid’s shorthanded breakaway at Boston on 18 December 2025, from the copy that ships with the package, so nothing here needs the network. nhl_goal_tracking(2025020534, 777) fetches the same frames.

library(bluelineR)
path <- system.file("extdata", "goal-2025020534-777.json.gz", package = "bluelineR")
frames <- read_goal_tracking(path, game_id = 2025020534, event_id = 777)
frames
#> # A tibble: 1,683 × 9
#>   frame  time entity_id is_puck player_id sweater_number team      x       y
#>   <int> <dbl>     <dbl> <lgl>       <dbl>          <dbl> <chr> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1     0         1 TRUE           NA             NA NA     77.9 -30.7  
#> 2     1     0      6001 FALSE     8480280              1 BOS   -87.3  -0.403
#> 3     1     0      6018 FALSE     8478401             18 BOS    81.0  -4.75 
#> 4     1     0      6028 FALSE     8477496             28 BOS    54.4  -0.288
#> 5     1     0      6039 FALSE     8479987             39 BOS    57.7  15.4  
#> 6     1     0      6073 FALSE     8479325             73 BOS    44.9 -25.2  
#> # ℹ 1,677 more rows

Each row is one object in one frame. x runs along the rink and y across it, in feet from centre ice, the frame the play-by-play uses: the nets are at x = -89 and +89. The puck is entity_id 1.

When it went in

The clip runs on past the goal, and the puck can sit at the other net when it starts or blip over the line before the real goal. goal_frame() wants it in the net, between the posts, two frames running, at the net the clip finishes at:

g <- goal_frame(frames)
g
#> [1] 99
frames[frames$frame == g & frames$is_puck, c("time", "x", "y")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>    time     x     y
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1   9.8 -89.6 0.989

How it was scored 

goal <- classify_goal(frames, team = "EDM", shot_type = "backhand")
t(goal[, c("shooter", "distance", "shot_speed", "since_neutral", "passes", "rush", "breakaway",
           "oddman", "onetimer", "cross", "traffic", "behind", "forecheck")])
#>                    [,1]
#> shooter       8478402.0
#> distance            7.5
#> shot_speed         24.1
#> since_neutral       2.8
#> passes              2.0
#> rush                1.0
#> breakaway           1.0
#> oddman              0.0
#> onetimer            0.0
#> cross               0.0
#> traffic             0.0
#> behind              0.0
#> forecheck           0.0

It was a rush (the puck was in Edmonton’s end 2.8 seconds before the shot) and a breakaway: McDavid carried it over the blue line with no Bruin but the goalie between him and the net. He shot from 7.5 feet; the puck left his stick at 24 mph, a backhand.

The rules in ?classify_goal are the ones BluelineMetrics builds its goal types with. On 120 goals from 2025-26 the R version agrees with the site’s on every type, the shooter, the distance, the shot speed and the number of passes.

How fast he was going

skater_speed() gives every skater’s speed at every frame, over the 0.6 seconds around it:

speed <- skater_speed(frames)
mcd <- speed[speed$player_id == 8478402, ]
round(max(mcd$speed_mph, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
#> [1] 20.3

Drawing it 

plot_goal(frames, title = "McDavid, shorthanded breakaway at Boston")

plot_goal_sequence(frames, n = 6, seconds = 5)

nhl_rink() is the empty rink, in the same feet, for drawing anything else on.
